testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When making a left turn, when should you start the turn?

options.text: Before you reach the center of the intersection.
At or after you reach the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels pass the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after you reach the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before you turn. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: When speeding up on a wet road, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about the road surface.

questions.explanation: Speed up very slowly when driving on wet roads or other surfaces with poor grip.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They are illegal in most states.
They let drivers see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
The brakes become soft and squishy.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and make the brakes fail.

questions.question: What is the maximum weight allowed on a single axle?
questions.explanation: In Washington State, no more than 20,000 pounds can be placed on any single axle of a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block other drivers, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and slow down traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank do?

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they have locked due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air brakes do not work instantly. It takes time for air to travel through the lines. Usually there is a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.

questions.question: What must a truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What is black ice?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, what is your best option to stop?
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for an escape ramp. An escape ramp is the safest way to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: A CMV driver with any detectable alcohol in their system (but below the legal limit) will receive:
questions.explanation: If you have any detectable alcohol in your system while driving a CMV, even if your blood alcohol is below 0.04%, you will be ordered out of service for 24 hours. It is illegal and dangerous to drive a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Not wearing a safety belt while driving is:
questions.explanation: You must always wear a safety belt when operating a commercial vehicle. Driving without a safety belt is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for multiple brake uses if the compressor stops working.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for multiple brake uses if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air so you can use the brakes several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items stand taller in a trailer.
Stop items from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing keep cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo. Bracing extends from the top of the cargo to the floor and walls to prevent movement.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can allow poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can allow poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into your cab or sleeper. Check your exhaust system regularly for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your wheels from locking up.
Prevent your vehicle from speeding on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Veer your trailer right and stop.
Veer your trailer left and stop.

questions.explanation: During an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Always brake in a straight line. This keeps your vehicle straight but still allows you to turn if needed.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior during the on-road test.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must keep ____ points of contact with the vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must also hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Before a trip, make sure that:

options.text: The grooved pedal surface has not been worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface has not been worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that nothing blocks the pedals. Make sure the pedals work properly and that grooved pedal surfaces are not smooth.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, decrease your speed.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose, soaked with oil or grease, or dangerously thin.

questions.question: When pulled over to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Rely on your taillights to alert other drivers.
Use your four-way emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way emergency flashers to alert other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road, especially when it is hard to see. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Stop cargo from being loaded too high.
Stop cargo from being unloaded too fast.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: A driver can rely on front wheel braking to work:
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. Front wheel skids are very unlikely, even on ice.

questions.question: A load that is 40 feet long should be secured by at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo needs at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: What is the maximum legal length for a double-trailer combination?
questions.explanation: In Washington State, double-trailer combinations cannot be longer than 61 feet.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?
questions.explanation: Use a B:C fire extinguisher for electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning light comes on in a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but continue if nothing seems wrong.

questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You need to maintain braking power to stop safely.

questions.question: You are driving slowly in a construction zone and see a worker near the road. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly through construction zones. Slow down further if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: When parking on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after you apply the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on a level surface. This is essential to keep the trailer from moving if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be hazardous?

options.text: People often hurry when leaving the trucks and may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out of trucks into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People often hurry when leaving the trucks and may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver may rush into traffic without warning or step out without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: What is a problem with rough acceleration?

options.text: It is a good way to stay awake on long trips.
It can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Rough acceleration damages the engine and transmission. Always accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: What happens if you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
The left side of your vehicle may hit other vehicles.
Other drivers will move their vehicles out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of your vehicle may hit other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reach the center of the intersection before starting your left turn. Turning too early causes the left side of your vehicle to swing into other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, what is required?

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear a safety belt when driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: What prevents wheels from locking up when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup when brakes are applied.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get a full night of sleep before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a full night of sleep before your trip.
questions.explanation: Tired driving is very dangerous. To prevent drowsiness, get enough sleep before driving, have someone ride with you, drive when you are normally awake, and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise also helps you stay awake while driving.

questions.question: What should you do to stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Ride with a second person who can share driving duties.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with a second person who can share driving duties.
questions.explanation: Sharing driving with another person reduces the risk of tired driving for both of you. You can also stay alert by eating light meals and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge is too hot, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the safe level, stop driving right away and find out what is wrong. A problem with your vehicle could cause engine failure or even a fire.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
The maximum weight a vehicle can tow
The minimum weight a vehicle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing your brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep your steering movements small while braking this way.

questions.question: What is the safe maximum air loss rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How should you brake when using ABS?

options.text: Brake the same way as you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as you normally do.
questions.explanation: When using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use your parking brake if your brakes are hot after coming down a steep hill. Wait for the brakes to cool before using the parking brake, or you may damage them.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how many seconds should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds. Check this during your vehicle inspection.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for the safe operation of a vehicle. Always perform routine inspections before driving a commercial motor vehicle.
